resources.string: XMPP chat for ATAK, based on Conversations
Enter your full XMPP address (user@server): no XMPP domain is configured
Signed in with the credentials of TAK server %1$s. To use another account, turn off \"Use TAK server credentials\" in the settings.
The XMPP connection is turned off in the TAK Convo settings.
No TAK server credentials are available. Add a TAK server with a username and password (Settings › Network Preferences › TAK Servers), or sign in with an XMPP account.

ATAK keeps your username for TAK server %1$s but not its password, for example after enrolling for a client certificate. Enter that password to sign in. TAK Convo keeps it in ATAK\'s encrypted credential store, and asks again only if the server refuses it.
The XMPP server refused the password you entered for TAK server %1$s, so TAK Convo won\'t try it again. Enter the password again, or the new one if it has changed.
No XMPP server is configured. Import a TAK Convo .pref file (it can come in a mission package), set the XMPP domain in the settings, or sign in with a full XMPP address.
Your TAK server username is not a valid XMPP address. Sign in with an XMPP account instead.
Use the ATAK callsign as nickname
Your XMPP nickname, shown to your contacts and in group chats, follows your ATAK callsign
New messages notify while the chats are closed. Leave off when the Conversations app on this device uses the same account: it notifies. ATAK\'s contacts show unread messages either way.
New messages play the notification sound
A row of preset buttons above the message field
Buttons above the message field, separated by |. A tap adds the text to the message. Empty: no buttons.

The XMPP server\'s certificate isn\'t trusted. By default TAK Convo trusts the certificate authorities of your TAK server connections: connect to your TAK server, or trust the device\'s CA store or a CA certificate file in the settings.
Sign out of %1$s? Its chat history stays on this device.
Waiting for you to approve the server

TAK Convo's server settings have changed, for example by an imported .pref file or data package. Connect only if you or your administrator changed them.

Server: %1$s
Signs in with: %2$s
Extra trusted certificates: %3$s
TAK Convo: approve the new server
The XMPP server settings changed. Chats stay offline until you approve the server or change the settings back.
Not connected yet: connecting to the XMPP server…
ATAK doesn\'t know your position yet
That group chat isn\'t open in TAK Convo anymore
TAK Convo can\'t send this to a group chat
No chats yet: start one in TAK Convo first
Could not send it to the chat
Chats with the XMPP address a TAK user advertises, in TAK Convo
Connect to the XMPP server and advertise this device\'s XMPP address to other TAK users
Log in with the username and password of your TAK server connection. Clear to sign in with an XMPP account instead.
Automatic: a TAK server on the XMPP server\'s domain, otherwise another one, connected ones first
The server part of your XMPP address, e.g. chat.example.org
Connect to this host instead of looking the domain up in DNS (leave empty normally)
Your XMPP server: the channels of its group chat services
The public directory search.jabber.network: public channels of the whole XMPP network. Your searches are sent to it.
A server (example.org) or its group chat service (conference.example.org)
Trust the certificate authorities of your TAK server connections (the truststores imported in ATAK). Public CAs are always trusted.
Also trust the certificate authorities installed on this device, including ones you imported (Settings › Security › Encryption and credentials) or an MDM installed
None: tap to trust a CA certificate file (.pem, .crt, .cer, .der)
Load these settings from a .pref file. A mission package can carry the same file.
No settings could be read from %1$s
The greyed-out settings come from your device management (MDM) and can\'t be changed here
A CA certificate from your device management
None, set by your device management
